channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Viral Handbags Turn Small Designer Into Fashion Star
item.description: New York Handbag Designer Pierre Laborde tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a viral TikTok video transformed his handmade leather bags from a longtime fixture at a local street market into a sought-after fashion accessory, with demand now exceeding his small team's production capacity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Laborde says he plans to preserve the individuality and craftsmanship of his designs rather than pursue mass production or partnerships with major retailers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: The growing debate over video calls on airplanes, premium California wines selling at steep discounts under supermarket private labels, a new rivalry between New York diners featuring singing waiters and the growing popularity of elaborate tuna carving experiences at high-end sushi restaurants. Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hurricane Isaias May Cost Insurers Billions
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Insurance Equity Analyst Matthew Palazola tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Hurricane Isaias could generate insured losses in the single-digit billions of dollars, with stronger Florida building codes potentially limiting damage despite rising property values. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Palazola says two relatively mild hurricane seasons have helped insurers rebuild capital, while recent Florida insurance reforms have improved market conditions but have yet to face a major test. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Plague Scare Raises Public Health Questions
item.description: Baylor College of Medicine Tropical Medicine Expert Dr. Peter Hotez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the unexplained death of a researcher at a Russian plague institute raises questions about a possible pneumonic plague infection, although there is no evidence of a wider outbreak or biological weapons activity. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Hotez calls for an independent World Health Organization investigation and warns that the US lacks adequate plague vaccine preparedness. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russian Diesel Deal Unlikely to Lower US Prices
item.description: Bloomberg Economics Economic Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump's agreement to obtain Russian diesel is unlikely to significantly lower US fuel prices because the proposed November shipment amounts to roughly one day of American consumption. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kennedy says damage to Russian refineries, logistical challenges and potential legal restrictions raise questions about whether Moscow can deliver the promised fuel, while the agreement could complicate Ukraine's campaign against Russian energy infrastructure. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banana Ball Takes Its Baseball Show Nationwide
item.description: Banana Ball Championship League Owner Jesse Cole tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Savannah Bananas have built a new kind of baseball experience around faster games, elaborate entertainment and affordable tickets, helping create a wait list of roughly 5 million fans. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Cole says the league plans to keep expanding its audience in the US and internationally while maintaining its fans-first model, including $35 tickets without added fees and free game streams on YouTube. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jefferies Says It Found Fraud in $900 Million of Radiant Deals
item.description: A Jefferies-run fund said in court proceedings that it has evidence of alleged fraudulent conduct by iron ore traders Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals in receivables-financing deals with a face value of almost $900 million.
item.dc:creator: Upmanyu Trivedi, Jack Farchy and Archie Hunter

item.title: Restaurant Theft Adds to Rising Dining Costs
item.description: Bloomberg Pursuits Food Editor Kate Krader tells Bloomberg This Weekend that diners are taking everything from silverware and glassware to artwork and bathroom fixtures, adding replacement costs for restaurants already struggling with tight profit margins. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Krader also discusses the return of late night dining in cities including New York and London as restaurants extend their hours and customers embrace later reservations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hurricane Isaias Slams Florida Panhandle
item.description: AccuWeather Correspondent Bill Wadell joins hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend from Pensacola Beach, Florida, where Hurricane Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 storm, bringing damaging winds, flooding and widespread power outages across the Gulf Coast. Wadell says the storm has weakened as it moves inland, but downed power lines, debris and continued flooding remain concerns as crews begin restoring electricity and assessing the damage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Draws Ukraine Criticism
item.description: Atlantic National Security Staff Writer Nancy Youssef tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump's agreement to import Russian diesel could provide limited relief from high fuel prices while potentially increasing Moscow's revenue as it continues its war in Ukraine. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Youssef also discusses Pentagon planning for possible new strikes against Iran and the challenges facing indirect negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz and a potential ceasefire. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why This Canadian Community Is Betting on Coal Again
item.description: A proposed metallurgical coal mine in Alberta’s Crowsnest Pass is reviving an old industry at a time when Canada is looking for new trade relationships beyond the United States. Northback Holdings says Grassy Mountain could supply steelmaking coal to customers in Europe and Asia while bringing jobs and investment back to a community that lost much of its mining economy. But opponents, including musician and activist Corb Lund, warn that the project could threaten water quality and surrounding communities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Poland Central Bank Faces Meeting Hurdles Without Glapinski: PAP
item.description: The potential suspension of Polish central bank governor Adam Glapinski could make it difficult to convene meetings of the rate-setting panel, a policymaker said, as an “unprecedented” legal challenge raises questions about the institution’s leadership.
item.dc:creator: Zosia Wanat

item.title: Rich Countries Are Now on Front Lines as World’s Risk Map Shifts
item.description: Typically called into action when poor countries get mired in debt, the International Monetary Fund will be confronted this week with mounting signs of trouble in the wealthiest ones.
item.dc:creator: Jorgelina do Rosario

item.title: China Passenger Vehicle Retail Sales Drop 24% in September
item.description: China’s passenger vehicle retail sales fell 24% in September from a year earlier to 1.702 million units, while new-energy vehicle sales declined 12% to 1.141 million units, according to data released by the China Passenger Car Association.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Banking Stock Swoon in Europe Is a Sign of Caution, Not Panic
item.description: A selloff in banking stocks is rarely comforting. But after three years of strong gains, the latest pullback in European lenders looks more like a reset than a crash.
item.dc:creator: Macarena Muñoz and Julien Ponthus

item.title: Taiwan’s Lai Urges Democracies to Unite After Trump-Xi Talks
item.description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te called on democracies in the region to unite against threats to stability, as the island faces pressure from Beijing and concerns that US President Donald Trump’s rapprochement with China could come at Taiwan’s expense.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: India Announces Emergency Steps to Support Plunging Currency
item.description: India’s central bank rolled out a series of measures to support the sliding rupee in its strongest action since the country’s currency crisis in 2013.
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Sircar, Pratigya Vajpayee and Bhaskar Dutta

item.title: Balancing Conviction and Risk: Masters in Business with Maria Vassalou
item.description: Barry speaks with Maria Vassalou, Head of the Pictet Research Institute. They discuss her research into global markets, and how they balance geopolitical risk. They also discuss China's growth as a technical innovator, and the risks to US debt. Finally, Barry and Maria discuss the differences between investing research and academia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Phenomenal Time To Be Investor, Not Consumer: Amoroso
item.description: Anastasia Amoroso, chief investment strategist with Partners Group, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the bullish sentiment in the stock market, the potential for volatility in the near future, and rising global yields. (Source: Bloomberg)
